items.name: Professor Metter's Terminal
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.text:
The open roads being no stranger to enterprising bands of marauders, I set upon locating a site suitable for our company's needs. And I found it. The Ash Cave, our new home. We required somewhere sheltered from the elements - the machinery we need demands it. Likewise, we needed protection. Protection from raiders who would seize our spoils, and from the aberrations who would rend us limb from limb.

Until such a time as we have armed and armored ourselves at scale, we must rely on the traditional fortification for our security needs. The wall, the tower, and the gate.  

The Ash Cave is ideal for our purposes. Its expansive dimensions shield us from most avenues of attack, and its high ceiling shields us from the sun and storm alike. Expanding upon it's natural defensive characteristics is entirely possible.

Improvement will take time, but they can be assembled. Its proximity to Athens provides ample opportunities for salvage runs - although I must caution my people not venture far into that wretched necropolis. Unless, of course, the equipment is worth it.

What is one of their lives worth when weighed against the integrated circuit?

Hardware is only one side of the equation. Survival demands that I do tend to the human element as well. The body, the will. The reliable, consistent, laboratory-repeatable instillation of fearlessness, trauma resistance, endurance, and reflexes are only produced by one source. Drugs.

I am going to require a sea of drugs.

Far more drugs than we can scavenge. We're going to need a laboratory of our own.

Sourcing the necessary active ingredients will hardly be my only challenge. I have to teach the art of chemical manufacturing in a way that doesn't encourage deviation or experimentation. We need steady results.

I've also got to convince the people that it is a common-sense necessity and a demonstration of of commitment to communal good to habitually flood one's body with psychoactive formula. That this is a natural, logical, aspect of the tempering that the Wasteland demands of us all.

We are likely to lose people in the process of securing the equipment and materials our manufacturing endeavors will require. Anything from we can only retrieve from Athens, in particular, will be very difficult to obtain.

While unfortunate, such sacrifices are necessary to ensure the people are no stranger to the laboratory's bounty.

To truly stand in Wasteland and to know that one has made of themself an enduring thing requires more than flesh. More than leather and hammered scrap. More even than interwoven ballistic fibers. True tempering requires power armor.

It demands a mastery of one's environment that rises from integrated environmental regulation systems, and from the miracles of materials science: layers of poly-laminate, ceramic composites, and assorted alloys.

It requires that one possess the capacity to plant oneself where one will and I proclaim "This is the air that I will breathe, and this is the ground upon which I will stand." The perfect imposition of one's will upon a broken world. Freedom. 

The ability to fuel these armors is all around us. In the air, in the tumult of the earth's breath itself. I have designed a network of windmills that allow us to recharge our precious fusion cores.

If we make both a tradition of the judicious use of armor and a crime of the frivolous waste of stored power, and if the windmills remain secure, then we should be able to adopt a doctrine that permits routine deployment of power armor.

We should be in a position to thrive.

Our walls are sound, and, aside from the occasional intrusion of a biological aberration, our territory is secure. The time has come to grow our number.
 
Perhaps one in ten of the dregs that wander to our gates, or are selected for recruitment by one of our salvage patrols will prove themselves hardy enough to stand among the people. 

Those that do not chafe at the chemical stains and rad burns of honest scrap-sorting will be given opportunities to distinguish themselves. Those who yet demonstrate a proclivity for focused violence and are able to maintain precision whilst adrift in the psychoactive sea that comes with tempering will be considered for the opportunity to bear a suit of power armor. 

Upon the death or perhaps untimely demise of it's current occupant, that is.
 
If you cannot survive in your armor, how could you claim to deserve it?

We've bodies enough now but find ourselves wanting for power armor. Tempering is hardly complete without it. Weapons are far easier to come by, and the people have become proficient at refurbishing damaged components and calibrating focusing arrays.

Military-grade power armor is more challenging to source, but our determination is dogged. Salvage patrols search for derelict army convoys, supply depots, and among the towns where martial law rose and fell. Scrapmongers strip robots and other electronics for viable components. 

Even the youngest among us, whom I refer to as greasetraps, are proud to use their tiny hands to apply lubrication to worn actuators. It brings me great happiness to see the people so united in purpose. 

In time, we will have assembled the most robust, and assuredly the most deadly, collection of functional power armors in all of southern Ohio. Soon, perhaps within a few years, the people will begin to shift priorities from provision and security to territorial expansion.

It is with a heavy heart that I confirm that Herman, my first and most loyal adherent, has developed what I must consider to a terminal case of mercy. He has made such impressive strides--the man he is today he is a far cry from the common brute I met outside of Athens several years ago.

And yet, I have received troubling reports.

That on patrols he often misses shots at unarmed targets. And I've run the numbers, the accuracy decline Herman exhibits in the case of defenseless targets is statistically significant. Shockingly, I've heard whispers that he has even permitted children encountered on salvage patrols to flee without even attempting mitigation.

Somehow, Herman's tempering has become undone. His mind is no longer sound. Given his status among our people, and the technical prowess he has developed, I have no choice but to consider him a serious threat. Not only to myself, but to our traditions.

To my legacy.

There isn't enough for everyone in the Wasteland, and there never will be. If you do not take, what is yours will be taken. Your valuables. Your life. Your home. To deny this fact, to show mercy to the stranger, is to betray one's people. It is intolerable. It is obscene.

Tomorrow at dawn I will declare Herman to be shattered, no longer tempered and no longer one of the people. He shall be stripped of his arms and armor and lashed to the rod outside of the aberration to the northeast's cave. His bones will serve as a warning to those who enter our territory, and to those who would allow the specter of clemency to dwell among their thoughts.

I've finally met this Rust King face to face and, I must say, he didn't disappoint. I have never met such a brutal specimen - indeed, he can hardly be called a man at all. He's impossibly large, he crushes poly-laminate composite with his bare hands, and his gaze misses no detail.

He has a natural affinity for savagery, elevating it almost to an art, and yet he is terribly clever. So, a man? I don't think so. Something greater.

There comes a time for even the strongest material to either bend or break. And there can be no real question that, for all our considerable might, the Rust King is stronger than we are.

I am ill. Dying, certainly. My condition has worsened considerably over the past few years. It cannot be hidden anymore, although most know better than to speak of it. Abraxodyne's errant product plays havoc within me. I do not expect to see the spring.

But, I am not afraid, I have outlived my home and have lived well. From blood, dust, and scrap, I have forged an enduring people. A future.

It is to preserve this legacy that I have decided that we will submit to the Rust King. To do otherwise is court a senseless, albeit spectacular, destruction. My people will live as they have, reaving, and building, and tempering, and our traditions will continue. My legacy will persist.

I will send word in the morning that I have accepted his terms, and that the Ash Cavers will join their ranks to his.

entries.title: Security Concerns
entries.text:
The guard posted at Windmill Gamma was found dead near her post. In her power armor. With her skull crushed. Through the helmet. 

The individual responsible for relieving the guard reported seeing an impossibly large man(?), with green-ish skin, heading away from our territory towards the south.

I inspected the guard's rifle. It had discharged at least three times recently. Troubling.  

This is the third "green man" sighting in as many months. I've heard it from scavenger crews, but I did not believe it. And now, it is on my doorstep. It appears something was probing our territory. Curious that it did not approach the camp. Could it be intelligent? 

Perhaps it is interested in the windmills? I order increased security details around each site. We can ill afford to lose them.

items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: 10/23/2077: Day One
entries.text:
We were on standard training maneuvers near Athens when the war began. I do not know who started it. I do not know who won. What I do know is that emergency preparedness protocols require that we redeploy to the nearby town of Athens. 

Our mission is to provide relief and maintain order until we are relieved. Beyond Athen's civil defense supplies, we have few resources. We have not been able to establish communications with my superiors, the Army, or the Governor. Civil authorities are in disarray. Athens lost its mayor in the first hour. A heart attack, I am told. Nobody can find the chief of police. I still can't contact Columbus or Cleveland. 

They might have been hit. I don't know.

For now, it seems we are on our own. Hopefully not for long. I am writing this log to help with the preparation of reports I expect to make when relief arrives.

entries.title: 10/25/2077: The Seismic Event
entries.text:
Unforeseen factors have severely impaired the security of Athens. A series of seismic events, almost certainly related to the atomic exchange, has disordered the very earth beneath us. Large cracks have compromised the integrity of many of the city's buildings. 

I am told that as the earth settles, the damage will compound. The topography of the town will be dramatically altered, perhaps to the point where whole sections collapse.

We may need to construct temporary pathways around the most damaged sections of town. The situation remains fluid. 

We still are in the process of assessing the damage to the city's infrastructure, her pipes. The water we need to survive. Preliminary reports are dire. There is no choice but to severely tighten rationing.

entries.title: 11/02/2077: Lockdown
entries.text:
Our scouting parties have returned with more bad news: widespread unrest, throngs of refugees, and devastating chemical contamination have transformed the region surrounding Athens into a waking nightmare. I worry about the air and I keep my face covered whenever possible. The countryside is covered in compromised farms. Fields of contaminated crops rot where they stand. 

The men I dispatched to Cleveland never returned. Same with Columbus.

Providing for the people already present in Athens threatens to overwhelm our already meager supplies. The sudden loss of a reliable water supply puts us in a situation where I cannot permit an influx of refugees. We have no running water. The additional strain would destabilize us. We can help them when relief arrives. Until then, I have to save what I can.

I've ordered the closure of Athens' borders: no one goes in or out without my authorization. I'm sympathetic to the fact that people have family members out there, that they're Americans. But we must be pragmatic.

The choice now is between either losing some or losing all the region's civilian population. No choice at all.

entries.title: 12/08/2077: Disposal
entries.text:
Considering Greer's report and given my own concerns about our ability to maintain order in Athens, I've made the difficult decision to implement immediate quarantine and corpse disposal protocols. We have no cure, no treatment. 

Containment is our only hope.

Incineration or exile of contaminated individuals is our only choice. If they prove to be violent we have no choice but to defend ourselves. For sanitation, we'll have to use makeshift burn pits, and we can't compromise our defensive perimeter.  So, we must conduct emergency disposal activities within the town itself.

This is a nightmare.

entries.title: 12/21/2077: Collapse
entries.text:
The situation in Athens has become untenable. We're at our breaking point and no one is coming to help us. We have no unspoiled food or uncontaminated water. Our medical resources are spent. Even extreme measures have failed to keep us safe from the unknown condition. Most of us have visible sores. Few have all of their hair. A couple of the men became violent and had to be burned.

We've lost control of the borders. Much of the civilian population has fled the city, deciding to take their chances outside. Morale is critically low. Collapse is imminent. I will remain behind, with whomever stays, to guard the armory, but I cannot order my men to stay and die in this wretched, poisoned ruin.

The best I can do now is ensure that the weaponry in our keeping plays no role in the savagery beyond these city limits. When I can't hold on anymore, I'll send someone away with the key.

History may judge me harshly. I truly am sorry. I did my best.

entries.title: Lieutenant Albert Palmer's Report
entries.text:
It all happened fast. The civilians were lined up at the river, and we were trying to keep them orderly, but one look and you could see they were half-crazy with thirst. Fear too, I think. The purifier those students rigged worked, but it was slow. I was at the front, so I couldn't hear what people were saying, but a lot of people were talking, they looked angry.

I saw a trickle of water coming out, and it looked good. Then, someone shouted that it was running out, that there wasn't going to be any water and the crowd broke. They pushed the guy carrying a bucket down. I saw the clean water spill. We told them to get back in line, fired into the air. It didn't work. 

The crowd surged, went for Private Kupowski and took his rifle. When they pulled it loose, we panicked. God help me, we opened fire. When the dust cleared, three civilians and Kupowski were dead. The purifier was damaged too. I don't know if it was just some ricochet, or that and some thrown bricks. But it took a few hits. Smoke was coming out of it. A lot of people ran. 

Then, suddenly, it was quiet. We were all just standing around this big broken thing. And everybody understood there wasn't going to be any more drinking water. Not for a long time. The fight went right out of us.

entries.title: Medical Officer Edwin Greer's Report
entries.text:
There appears to be an unknown medical condition appearing throughout the region. I've reviewed about a dozen reports, and, before we burned him, the cadaver of the unidentified individual, the mailman, that was sanctioned on Court Street yesterday.

Like we talked about, the symptoms are shocking. Necrosis, hair loss, sores, discolored dermis. Neurological deterioration. I don't know what this is. Not a traditional disease. In some ways, it resembles radiation poisoning. In other ways, it's like nothing I've ever encountered. I haven't seen an indication that affected people are contagious, but I can't rule it out.

Whatever the cause, it is clear that affected individuals show alarming signs of psychological instability. Psychotic episodes and violent outbursts. Their horrific appearance threatens to upend public order. Bluntly, their mere presence will incite panic. 

I don't know how this happened. What I do understand is that under no circumstances can we allow this condition to gain a foothold in Athens. Panic aside, we don't have the resources to study it, much less treat it. We must contain it and stamp it out wherever we find it. Quarantine those who show symptoms and keep them out of sight until you can remove them from the city as quickly and as quietly as possible. Burn the dead to prevent further contamination.

Put those who become a danger to themselves or others down. They are beyond help.

In my capacity as a medical officer, I encourage you to protect the health of the civilian population, and the lives of your men, by any means necessary. Even those if those means seem barbaric. 

These are cruel days, Richard. They're getting crueler by the hour.

entries.title: Private Wendy Vanderman's Report
entries.text:
For the past few days, I've seen them gathering at the edges of our perimeter. Right before nightfall. Even through the scope it's hard to get a clear look, they stick to the brush and dart between vehicles.  Something seems wrong with them. The way they move. Their skin appears to be discolored.

Like the mailman that came into town.

It looks like they're watching the town. Their numbers are increasing steadily. I don't know what they're doing. I recommend that we prepare to repel an attack. 

I am requesting permission to fire at will, in case things change quickly.

entries.title: Dino Peaks Franchise Introduction
entries.text:
Welcome to the Dino Peaks Franchise Family! We are thrilled to invite you into the Mid-West's fastest growing Miniature Golf franchise. 

While you get things off the ground, please keep the following guidelines in mind:

-- Only use equipment and decorations provided by approved vendors. It's important that our brand consistency for quality shines through!

-- Remember the "difficulty recommendations" you were provided in advance of construction. Keep it fun, but frustrating! Your quota a free yearly pass awards will be closely monitored. Dino Peaks Franchisee Management retains the rights to enforce mandatory course redesigns if difficulty quotas are not met.

-- Ensure all staff is educated on the in's and out's of the franchise: everyone must remember the names of our Dino pal mascots:

Bogey the Dinosaur, Ace the Tee Rex, Birdie the Bronto, Parker the Triceratops, and of course, Clive.

-- Employees are forbidden from arguing dinosaur facts with customers. They are always right, even if they can't tell a Pterodactyl from a Pteranodon!

-- Last but not least: keep the park clean and safe! This should go without saying.

Please direct any questions of Dino Peaks Corporate HQ.

entries.text:
This terminal belongs to the University! It contains important research and studies of native plants and has no value to you! entries.title: Message From the Board
entries.text:
Miles,

Congratulations on your promotion! Know that we have every confidence in your capabilities. The Forever Farm is an important R&D initiative and your selection as facility manager is a great honor. It is our hope that this facility proves that the brightest star in subterranean agriculture's future is Abraxodyne's. I'm sure we don't need to remind you of the substantial investment we've made in this site, and in you as well.

Warmest Regards,

Your Friends on the Board

entries.title: Lockdown Hogwash
entries.text:
Miles Humphrey : Facility Manager's Log : 10/24/77

I don't understand how this happened. My terminal is supposed to be the only one that can place this facility under lockdown and even then I'd need permission from a board member to do it. There must be some kind of computer problem. I'll ask Carter to figure it out. He's a technical guy, after all.

entries.title: Authorization Denied???
entries.text:
Miles Humphrey : Facility Manager's Log : 10/28/77 

When I get out of here heads are going to roll. I should be able to open the lockdown. I'm the facility manager. What I say goes. I never even heard of the "Green Thumb" protocol. Is this some kind of prank? Somebody's to spend the rest of their career scrubbing chemical vats in a northern Alaskan plant before this is settled.

entries.title: I Eat What I Want to Eat
entries.text:

Veronica needs to remember who answers to who. If I say we can eat the corn, then we can eat the corn. I'm not going to sit here and starve. I'm the manager and I call the shots in here.

entries.title: They Lied to Us?
entries.text:
Veronica Ramos : Security Officer's Log : 12/15/77

I caught Fox, our filtration engineer, muttering to himself in the pump room. That was yesterday. Today, he broke his right hand pounding on the outer door in an attempt to open it. 

Doc asked me to double check the reports myself and see if I can determine what is happening. If the system is lying, and if it's related to the illnesses we're seeing, then I need to find out. I need to understand exactly how bad our situation is.

entries.title: Weird guy - 09.02.2075
entries.text:
We got a visitor after the delivery yesterday. Said his name was Michael, and he was here "regarding" the 50 barrels that we don't know what to do with. Told us just to bury them deep, along with the food sanitizers, and not to put them close to anything important. 
We were instructed not to record their delivery and to delete any existing records.

We're also not to discuss him or anything he said with anyone... including the boss!

I don't know what this means, but I'm not getting in trouble for it. I'll keep the manifest under Admin access, just in case.

entries.title: Weird guy (again) - 03.03.2076
entries.text:
Michael came back again, same lecture as last time. 
I still don't know what we're supposed to do with these barrels 

The last batch started leaking and quickly killed off all of the surrounding plants, we had to dig them back up and move them again.

Whatever it is, it's leaving stains on the rocks, the tools... even the dirt. I guess we just keep burying them and hope it doesn't spill out again.

items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: My Diary
entries.text:
Dear Diary,

So I'm giving this a try, I guess. I was told writing things down might help me "process" everything, whatever that means. Here goes. 

Today I shot and killed a woman who tried to steal some of the armor. I felt nothing. Actually, no, that's a lie. I was irritated because I had to dispose of the body, because the Deathclaws had already been fed. 

I don't know how writing that down is supposed to help, honestly, other than highlighting the fact I killed someone today, and all I felt was irritation at the inconvenience.

This sucks. Writing this down isn't helping; it's just made me realize that the only thing I have to talk to is this terminal. It's also shown me that I've become exactly like the animals that put me in this position in the first place.

I think I'll just bottle it all up in the future and grab a bounty if it gets too much. I'll either feel better, or someone will take me out. Win-win.

entries.title: Weird guy (again) - 03.03.2076
entries.text:
Michael came back again, same lecture as last time. 
I still don't know what we're supposed to do with these barrels 

The last batch started leaking and quickly killed off all of the surrounding plants, we had to dig them back up and move them again.

Whatever it is, it's leaving stains on the rocks, the tools... even the dirt. I guess we just keep burying them and hope it doesn't spill out again.

entries.title: Staff Reminders | October 2077
entries.text:
Reminders for the month:

1. Staff are required to wear the provided Halloween costumes for film screenings. A fear of clowns doesn't excuse you from your responsibilities to the Starlight Drive-In.

2. Projectionists must double-check the projector before screenings and complete regular maintenance every day.

3. Concessions staff need to push add-on sales of Nuka-Cola and popcorn; their mark-ups keep us in business.

Let's make this October the scariest one yet!

William Knight
Manager

items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: New Purchasing Rules
entries.text:
Harley 

We need to reduce costs across the board. Deliveries will be reduced from every two days down to once a week. 

Tell the staff to stop throwing out anything that's past its sell by date that still looks good, (those dates are suggestions anyway). If it isn't rotten, sell it.
 
Only reorder stock when we are down to the last box. If purchasing costs continue to rise, staff hours may need to be rethought up to and including layoffs. 

Management.

entries.title: Super-Duper Discount Club Reminder
entries.text:
Attention all associates!
 
Be sure to remind customers about the Super-Duper Discount Club during checkout. Membership gets them 10% off storewide, plus this week's exclusive offer:
 
Buy 2 Abraxo Cleaner products, get 1 free!
 
Let's keep those savings super.
Management.

entries.title: Response to complaints
entries.text:
Attention all associates!

Customers are this store's lifeblood and therefore we should do whatever it takes to ensure they continue to visit our store. 

If customers return goods which were past sell by date at time of purchase, push exchanges over refunds and if the item is not open put it back on the shelf.

If customer's demand to speak to management, have Bill talk to them; he has a way with problem customers. Refunds should be a last resort.

Management.

entries.title: William
entries.text:
Strong leadership qualities. Runs the store well, deals with problem customers easily, and follows instructions without question so long as he is paid well. 
Get him whatever he needs. He keeps a tight ship because staff 'respect' him; piss him off and the staff will do what he asks them to. Do not get on his bad side: whatever raise he asks for, approve it.

entries.title: Florence
entries.text:
Typical lazy teen. Seems like Juvie scared her straight, not much fight in her despite occasionally giving customers attitude. 
Recommend reducing hours.

entries.title: Kane
entries.text:
Caught him hanging around "restocking" near the checkouts regularly during his shifts. 
Not sure if he's flirting with the cashier's or waiting for an opportunity. No cash missing as of yet. 
Sending a report to his parole officer just in case. I also recommend not having Kane working same shift as Florence.

entries.title: Xander
entries.text:
Good worker. Works fast, knows the warehouse inside and out, doesn't complain about hours or pay. 
Offer to put him on salary at a 2% increase of current hourly pay, then increase his hours.

entries.title: Matilda
entries.text:
Record is squeaky clean but I've got reports from Lola about medicines going missing from the pharmacy after Matilda's shifts. 
When asked about it she claimed she was disposing of expired medicines. 
I had Xander go through the trash to prevent loss of product. Have Lola move the products while Matilda is on shift. 
It will be cheaper to keep her part time than fire her and train a replacement. Keep an eye on this one.

entries.text:

              --------------------------

I have started to notice that the trucks are bringing smaller and smaller deliveries to the diner. 

Before, they would load off around three pallets, but now we're lucky if it's even one.

entries.title: Concerns Log Date: 07/02/77
entries.text:
--------------------------
              |        Notice          | 
              --------------------------
During closing hours, I managed to get another chance at continuing my investigation. 

To my surprise, the dumpster had been deep cleaned with chemicals and bleach, removing any trace of blood or animal remains that may have ended up left in there. 

I decided to walk close to the basement entrance and this awful stench seemed to leak through the gaps of the door. 
Due to the horrific smell, nausea and dizziness washed over me forcing me to seek fresh air.

entries.title: Concerns Log Date: 07/12/77
entries.text:
--------------------------
              |        Concern         | 
              --------------------------

I do worry if the business is going under, especially with their daughter's health as their main priority. It can't be easy.

That being said, they did seem oddly cheerful last time I saw them. Wouldn't stop rambling on about some new pie recipe, which got me thinking: how are they feeding that many customers with so little supplies? It's strange, and I think it's worth looking into. Not that I'm a tattle-tale, or anything.

items.name: Tales of the Rust Kingdom
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: Behold the King
entries.text:
Used to live in Athens before the world went to shit. A group of us took our chances in the Wasteland; it was kill or be killed, but we got used to it pretty quick. This one guy, Steve, used to be pretty timid but later got hooked on Psycho. 

Long story short, we got surrounded one night by the Rust King's men and they kicked our asses. I remember seeing him for the first time, this towering goliath. Three of us survived the initial fight; me, Steve, and one other guy who tried pleading for his life. In response, the Rust King crushed the guy's head with his bare hands. Then the King looked at me and Steve and just said "Fight".

All I remember is crushing Steve's skull with a rock. The rush I felt then was intense, I felt alive. I fought with all my might and proved myself worthy to live. The Rust King's way of life, it spoke to me and it's how I live my life now.

entries.title: Home
entries.text:
The Rust King isn't like a normal man, he's unafraid of radiation poisoning or death. Raiders followed him for his strength and slowly his army grew. Rumors of a nest of Deathclaws in the old Abraxodyne Chemical plant spread so the Rust King went to conquer.

Upon entering, the Deathclaws attacked. The fight was brutal, many died and the Rust King sustained wounds that would've killed lesser men. With a gouged eye and bleeding chest, the Rust King fought the Matriarch, eventually breaking its neck and tearing its head off. 

Any surviving Deathclaw fled into the Wasteland, abandoning the nest. The eggs left in the nest later became the first of the Rust Kingdom's conquered Deathclaws.

entries.title: Siege of Fort Steuben
entries.text:
One day, our scouts came across Fort Steuben, a stronghold overlooking the roads to the north-east. The Rust King understood the strategic importance of this location, so he sent a war party to conquer the bulwark. 

Fort Steuben's inhabitants were given a chance; to join us or die. They decided to fight. They fought hard, even managing to restore the old wall cannons. The battle lasted from the evening till dawn. 

Eventually the Rust King's men tore down their defenses and breached the fort, killing all that resisted and sending the survivors to the Arena. The stronghold was conquered.

entries.title: Fortifying our land
entries.text:
We've taken over most of Ohio, eventually reaching the river bordering Appalachia. Although we could easily conquer it, the Rust King was focused on Burning Springs.

Scouts were sent to survey the land. Only one returned and was infected with a strange sickness. Green crystals poked out their body and they became rabid like a wild dog. The King commanded a wall be built within the canyon entrance to keep out any and all people from Appalachia. 

In the end; a mighty fortress was constructed to signify the Rust Kingdom's border. Any outside threats would be put down before it even reached its walls!

items.name: World of Corn Administrator Terminal
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: Your Objective
entries.text:
As administrator, it is your objective to advance the public relations interests of Abraxodyne Chemical and secure a competitive advantage for Abraxodyne's agricultural portfolio by instilling a sense of brand loyalty within the next generation of Americans. 

By aligning our products with civic ideals, traditional family values, and national security, we make any competing brands and organizations implicitly suspect. Internal research suggests a direct relationship between the age of inducement of positive brand sentiment and the amount of advertising dollars required to maintain levels of positive sentiment over that consumer's life.

In other words, we'll save big in the long run if we reach youth as early as possible.

entries.title: Bright Future
entries.text:
This place is the perfect springboard for me. It's not just some roadside attraction, like Anderson said. It's a goldmine. From the moment they walk in to the moment they leave, kids are immersed in the Abraxodyne message. If this place achieves the desired effect on consumer sentiment, and I'm sure it will, I'm due a promotion to upper management. Kids leave here feeling safe. Safe because Abraxodyne keeps them safe.

And I've got ideas. The kind of ideas that belong in the corner office. I'll recommend that the board consider similar ventures highlighting personal hygiene, kitchen safety, and the importance of cleaning products to the military and national security. Under my supervision, of course.

entries.title: Cobby's Appeal
entries.text:
Internal focus group tests are bullish on Cobby's appeal. The reports indicate that he's going be a hit with children ages four through twelve.

The numbers are great. 90% of youth leaving the World of Corn regard Abraxodyne in highly favorable terms, up from 60% before visiting.  80% of respondents indicate that they feel safe with Cobby and would likely spend more time with him.

The boys in advertising are workshopping a radio serial about the adventures of Cobby, his friends, and their travels to lands in desperate need of agricultural support and American know-how. Maybe they can snap up some commercial airtime during The Silver Shroud? My kids love that one.

entries.title: Bandits vs Pests
entries.text:
Positive sentiment towards Abraxodyne increases by 5% when the word "pest" is replaced by the word "bandit." 

My immediate recommendations for further refinement of youth messaging for our agricultural suite assets:

-Leaning further into pesticide as enforcer of fairness and equity. Stopping the freeloader from robbing the honest farmer.

-Emphasize the dangers removed by Abraxodyne
products. Cultivate a sense of safety and gratitude.

-Stress that foods treated with Abraxodyne products taste better and provide more nutrition.

-Downplay any safety concerns as un-American.

items.name: World of Corn Visitor Terminal
items.lead: A terminal you can read in the world.

entries.title: The Miracle of Corn
entries.text:
Today, you'll learn all about the miraculous plant we call "corn" and the many wonders found within!

Did you know that man has treasured corn since ancient times? Corn is more than food - it's used in almost every part of lives! Did you know some makeup contains corn? Corn helps you look your best. Feeling under the weather? There may be corn in the medicine you need!

But who makes corn grow so strong and tall, and who keeps corn safe from nature's bandits, such as slugs and grasshoppers? Who guards our health and prosperity? 

Why America's farmers do of course, with a little help from their friends at Abraxodyne Chemical!

entries.title: Meet Cobby!
entries.text:
Cobby is your guide to the World of Corn!

Follow his lead as he takes you on an unforgettable tour of a magical realm. Marvel as he patrols the cornfield, ever watchful for bandits that would threaten America's corn! 

Listen carefully: Cobby is as wise as he is vigilant. He knows all there is to know about corn! You'll hardly believe your ears as a whole World of Corn unfolds before you!

Join him in the field!

entries.title: Museum Rules
entries.text:
We hope you enjoy your visit to the World of Corn. Please:

- Do not touch the museum exhibits

- Do not use flash photography

- Do not touch or push Cobby

- Do not engage in horseplay

- Do not chew gum

- Do not climb on the corn
